extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers and practitioners who create, publish, distribute, or use datasets (dataset creators, curators, and downstream model developers)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical guideline (a set of questions) for documenting datasets used in machine learning, covering motivation, composition, collection, preprocessing, distribution, maintenance, and legal/ethical considerations so users can assess appropriateness, limitations, and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why was the dataset created?
rubrics_metrics.description: Why was the dataset created? (e.g., were there specific tasks in mind, or a specific gap that needed to be filled?)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the motivation and intended task(s) for which the dataset was created so practitioners can judge appropriateness for other uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other possible/unsuitable tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: What (other) tasks could the dataset be used for? Are there obvious tasks for which it should not be used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List plausible alternative uses and explicit misuses or tasks the dataset is not suitable for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior uses and result links
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the dataset been used for any tasks already? If so, where are the results so others can compare (e.g., links to published papers)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide citations, links, and summaries of experiments run on the dataset to enable comparison and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Who funded the creation of the dataset? If there is an associated grant, provide the grant number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources and grant identifiers to reveal potential incentives, constraints, or obligations influencing dataset creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: General comments (motivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments? (Motivation section)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all field for extra contextual notes about the dataset's purpose or creation rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are the instances?
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the instances? (that is, examples; e.g., documents, images, people, countries) Are there multiple types of instances? (e.g., movies, users, ratings; people, interactions between them; nodes, edges)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the fundamental unit(s) of the dataset and whether multiple instance types are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationships between instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Are relationships between instances made explicit in the data (e.g., social network links, user/movie ratings, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether edges, links, or other inter-instance relations are included or must be inferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instance counts
rubrics_metrics.description: How many instances of each type are there?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts, cardinalities, and any relevant breakdowns (e.g., number of nodes/edges, number of images/labels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-instance data contents and labels
rubrics_metrics.description: What data does each instance consist of? “Raw” data (e.g., unprocessed text or images)? Features/attributes? Is there a label/target associated with instances? If the instances are related to people, are subpopulations identified (e.g., by age, gender, etc.) and what is their distribution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe raw vs derived fields, features, labels, and any demographic or subpopulation annotations and distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependency on external resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Is everything included or does the data rely on external resources? (e.g., websites, tweets, datasets) If external resources, a) are there guarantees that they will exist, and remain constant, over time; b) is there an official archival version. Are there licenses, fees or rights associated with any of the data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether resolution of external references is required, archival guarantees, and legal/usage constraints on referenced content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended splits and evaluation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there recommended data splits or evaluation measures? (e.g., training, development, testing; accuracy/AUC)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide canonical train/validation/test splits and recommended metrics to encourage consistent evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial experiments and baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: What experiments were initially run on this dataset? Have a summary of those results and, if available, provide the link to a paper with more information here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize baseline experiments, performance numbers, and pointers to papers or result pages for benchmarking.

rubrics_metrics.name: General comments (composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments? (Dataset composition)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free-form space for composition-related clarifications, caveats, or notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: How was the data collected?
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the data collected? (e.g., hardware apparatus/sensor, manual human curation, software program, software interface/API; how were these constructs/measures/methods validated?)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe collection mechanisms, instruments, scraping methods, APIs, human annotation processes, and validation steps for measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants in collection and compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Who was involved in the data collection process? (e.g., students, crowdworkers) How were they compensated? (e.g., how much were crowdworkers paid?)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose roles of people involved, recruitment, and compensation to assess labor ethics and potential quality effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Over what time-frame was the data collected? Does the collection time-frame match the creation time-frame?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide collection dates and discuss temporal consistency between data collection and dataset creation/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: How were per-instance items acquired or inferred?
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the data associated with each instance acquired? Was the data directly observable (e.g., raw text, movie ratings), reported by subjects (e.g., survey responses), or indirectly inferred/derived from other data (e.g., part of speech tags; model-based guesses for age or language)? If the latter two, were they validated/verified and if so how?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain provenance of each field: observed, self-reported, or inferred; include validation procedures for derived fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage: population vs sample
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the dataset contain all possible instances? Or is it, for instance, a sample (not necessarily random) from a larger set of instances?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether dataset is exhaustive or sampled and implications for generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: If sample: population and sampling strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dataset is a sample, then what is the population? What was the sampling strategy (e.g., deterministic, probabilistic with specific sampling probabilities)? Is the sample representative of the larger set (e.g., geographic coverage)? If not, why not (e.g., to cover a more diverse range of instances)? How does this affect possible uses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe target population, sampling method, known biases, and their likely impact on downstream uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing information and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there information missing from the dataset and why? (this does not include intentionally dropped instances; it might include, e.g., redacted text, withheld documents) Is this data missing because it was unavailable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List omitted fields or withheld records, reasons for missingness, and whether missingness is systematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Known errors, noise, redundancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any known errors, sources of noise, or redundancies in the data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document discovered bugs, label noise, duplicates, OCR errors, or other quality issues and their scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: General comments (collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments? (Data collection process)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional notes or caveats about collection procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: What preprocessing/cleaning was done?
rubrics_metrics.description: What preprocessing/cleaning was done? (e.g., discretization or bucketing, tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, SIFT feature extraction, removal of instances, processing of missing values, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail all transforms applied to raw data including filtering, normalization, tokenization, redaction, and instance removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Was raw data preserved?
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the “raw” data saved in addition to the preprocessed/cleaned data? (e.g., to support unanticipated future uses)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether original/raw artifacts are retained and how to access them to enable re-processing or different pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is preprocessing software available?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the preprocessing software available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether scripts, code, or pipelines used for preprocessing are publicly available (and provide links) to enable reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: General comments (preprocessing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments? (Data preprocessing)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extra notes on preprocessing rationale, limitations, or warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the collection meet original motivation?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this dataset collection/processing procedure achieve the motivation for creating the dataset stated in the first section of this datasheet?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-assess whether the realized dataset matches its original goals and note any gaps or deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Were people informed and consented?
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dataset relates to people (e.g., their attributes) or was generated by people, were they informed about the data collection? (e.g., datasets that collect writing, photos, interactions, transactions, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain notice/consent procedures, whether participants were told how data would be used, and any consent mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical obligations for other protected subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: If it relates to other ethically protected subjects, have appropriate obligations been met? (e.g., medical data might include information collected from animals)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document domain-specific ethical safeguards (animal-care protocols, facility approvals) when non-human subjects are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical review and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: If it relates to people, were there any ethical review applications/reviews/approvals? (e.g. Institutional Review Board applications)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose IRB/ethics committee reviews, approvals, protocol identifiers, or reasons why none were sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent details and revocation mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If it relates to people, were they told what the dataset would be used for and did they consent? What community norms exist for data collected from human communications? If consent was obtained, how? Were the people provided with any mechanism to revoke their consent in the future or for certain uses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide consent wording, consent modality (opt-in/opt-out), and any mechanisms for subjects to withdraw or restrict future uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for harm and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: If it relates to people, could this dataset expose people to harm or legal action? (e.g., financial social or otherwise) What was done to mitigate or reduce the potential for harm?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess risks (re-identification, harassment, legal exposure) and describe redaction, aggregation, access controls, or other mitigation steps taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias and disparate impact
rubrics_metrics.description: If it relates to people, does it unfairly advantage or disadvantage a particular social group? In what ways? How was this mitigated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document observed or potential demographic disparities, fairness analyses, and mitigation strategies applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: If it relates to people, were they provided with privacy guarantees? If so, what guarantees and how are these ensured?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify privacy-preserving techniques (anonymization, differential privacy), their parameters, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the dataset comply with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)? Does it comply with any other standards, such as the US Equal Employment Opportunity Act?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State compliance or non-compliance with applicable laws and standards; explain gaps and jurisdictional applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive or confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the dataset contain information that might be considered sensitive or confidential? (e.g., personally identifying information)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List sensitive fields, PII, medical/financial identifiers, and any protections or redactions applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate or offensive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the dataset contain information that might be considered inappropriate or offensive?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate presence of profanity, hate speech, sexually explicit content, and whether filters or content warnings are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: General comments (legal & ethical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments? (Legal & Ethical considerations)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional ethical reflections, community norms, or legal caveats not captured above.

rubrics_metrics.name: How is the dataset distributed?
rubrics_metrics.description: How is the dataset distributed? (e.g., website, API, etc.; does the data have a DOI; is it archived redundantly?)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide distribution channels, persistent identifiers (DOI), mirrors, and archival information for discoverability and longevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release date and canonical reference
rubrics_metrics.description: When will the dataset be released/first distributed? (Is there a canonical paper/reference for this dataset?)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State first release date and canonical citation to enable correct attribution and historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses, copyrights, and legal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: What license (if any) is it distributed under? Are there any copyrights on the data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State license terms, permitted uses, attribution requests, and any third-party copyrights affecting reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent & norms re: distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: If it relates to people, were they told what the dataset would be used for and did they consent? What community norms exist for data collected from human communications? If consent was obtained, how? Were the people provided with any mechanism to revoke their consent in the future or for certain uses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Repeated in distribution context) Clarify whether distribution is compatible with consent and community expectations, and whether revocation is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and access/export restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any fees or access/export restrictions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State cost, licensing fees, access controls, gated/approved releases, geo-export restrictions, or institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: General comments (distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments? (Dataset distribution)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Miscellaneous distribution-related notes (mirror policies, embargoes, citation requests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who maintains and hosts the dataset?
rubrics_metrics.description: Who is supporting/hosting/maintaining the dataset? How does one contact the owner/curator/manager of the dataset (e.g. email address, or other contact info)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institution/organization/individual responsible, hosting URL, and contact information for support and queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update policy and errata
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the dataset be updated? How often and by whom? How will updates/revisions be documented and communicated (e.g., mailing list, GitHub)? Is there an erratum?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe versioning policy, release cadence, channels for change announcements, and location of errata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obsolescence communication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dataset becomes obsolete how will this be communicated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify deprecation notices, archival procedures, or migration plans to notify users about obsolescence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository of works using the dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a repository to link to any/all papers/systems that use this dataset?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide curated lists or links to publications, benchmarks, or leaderboards that use the dataset to aid users in evaluation context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism for extensions and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: If others want to extend/augment/build on this dataset, is there a mechanism for them to do so? If so, is there a process for tracking/assessing the quality of those contributions. What is the process for communicating/distributing these contributions to users?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe contribution workflows, quality control, provenance tracking, and how community-driven extensions are integrated or distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: General comments (maintenance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other comments? (Dataset maintenance)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for maintenance-related notes and long-term stewardship considerations.
